 Sanremo Festival 2027: dates, tickets and where to stay 
 Destinations Sanremo Festival 2027 : dates, tickets and where to stay
 Dates of the Sanremo Festival 2027, tickets, where to stay, trains from Nice, Milan and Paris, and what the town offers without a ticket. Sourced and dated.
 Updated November 16, 2026 
 19 min read 
 Contents
 Loading… 
 Commercial partnership . This article contains affiliate links. If you book through these links, Pixidia earns a small commission at no extra cost to you. Partners: Viator The Sanremo Festival 2027 runs from Tuesday 16 to Saturday 20 February 2027, over five evenings at the Teatro Ariston. The rules published by Rai on 21 September 2026 set these dates, but the 2027 ticket sale has no confirmed day yet. Without a ticket, you can still experience the Festival around town.
 Checked on 16 November 2026 against the sources cited at the end of this article, including the Rai rules as reported by the press. 
 Sanremo is more than one hall. Every February, the Riviera dei Fiori hosts Italy’s most-watched song contest, and the whole town changes pace for five evenings. The Teatro Ariston, which has hosted the Festival since 1977, holds about 2,000 seats in 2026, and many of them go to guests, sponsors and industry professionals. For the general public, the hall is hard to get into. This guide starts from that reality: what you can do without a ticket, what the 2027 rules change, what tickets, accommodation and trains cost, and what the sources don’t yet say.
 1. Experiencing the Festival without a ticket, in town
 Photo by Annie Spratt on Unsplash Sanremo, a town that spills over into the Festival
 16 to 20 February 2027 
 February: about 8 to 13°C 
 Free concerts in 2026 
 Centre on foot The Festival doesn’t stay inside the Ariston. During the week, Via Matteotti, the streets of the centre and the seafront take over, with screens, music and fans waiting for the artists. In 2026, the Green Carpet, the red carpet that links the Palafiori to the Ariston, ran on Monday 23 February in Via Matteotti, according to the Italian press of the time. For 2027, no programme for these events has been published: what follows describes the 2026 edition, which is a benchmark rather than a guarantee.
 Highlights on foot
 La Pigna, Sanremo’s old medieval quarter, can be explored entirely on foot from the centre. The writer Italo Calvino grew up there. 
 Piazza Colombo hosted free concerts from Tuesday to Saturday in 2026, on the Suzuki stage, according to Italpress. 
 Corso Imperatrice, the seafront promenade that starts at the Casinò, is lined with palm trees and a marble pavement. A Russian Orthodox church stands along this route. 
 Pixidia tip: without a ticket, plan your days around the town rather than the Ariston. Check the day’s events on the day itself, because the 2027 programme has not been published. A day without a ticket, step by step
 Here’s a plan that follows the 2026 format. In the morning, walk up to La Pigna from the centre. At midday, stop by the flower market, which fits the town’s nickname. Its opening hours have not been checked, so ask locally before you go. In the afternoon, walk down Corso Imperatrice to the Casinò, then head back toward the centre. In the evening, Piazza Colombo can be your meeting point if the free concerts return in 2027.
 If you want a clear thread for your visit, a food tour is the easiest format to fit around the Festival. The Sanremo Food Tour, which lasts 3 to 4 hours according to its listing, mixes Ligurian street food with the medieval old town. On the Viator listing checked on 16 November 2026, it showed departures on 16, 19 and 20 February 2027; the 17th and 18th were not among the dates checked. Availability can change before February, so recheck before you lock in your stay.
 Sanremo Food Tour: authentic Ligurian street food and medieval town ★ 4.9 · 39  reviews Partner link 
€95 per adult (€190 for 2 adults, checked on 16 November 2026)
 €95 per adult (€190 for 2 adults, checked on 16 November 2026) 
 See dates 2. The 2027 calendar: five evenings, and a format that changes
 What the rules published on 21 September 2026 set
 16 to 20 February 2027 
 5 evenings 
 24 artists 
 Stefano De Martino Rai published the rules on 21 September 2026, as reported by Sorrisi and LaPresse . Stefano De Martino hosts the Festival and serves as its artistic director. The format runs for five evenings, Tuesday to Saturday, with three highlights: the cover night on Thursday 18, the performance night on Friday 19 and the final night on Saturday 20.
 What changes compared with previous editions
 The performance night on Friday 19 selects Italy’s representative for the Eurovision Song Contest 2027. 
 The public can vote online via RaiPlay, up to three votes per user. Outside Italy, sources disagree on access to RaiPlay; no official information exists for 2027. 
 Songs written by an artificial intelligence are banned by the rules. 
 Pixidia tip: the weighting of online votes is not confirmed in the sources we read, so this article gives no percentages. Festival of Sanremo 2027 schedule, according to the rules published on 21 September 2026 Evening Date What the rules say, according to the press 
 First evening Tuesday 16 February 2027 First of the five evenings; content not detailed in the sources we read 
 Second evening Wednesday 17 February 2027 Programme evening; format not detailed in the sources we read 
 Cover night Thursday 18 February 2027 Cover song night 
 Performance night Friday 19 February 2027 Selects Italy’s representative for Eurovision 2027 
 Final evening Saturday 20 February 2027 Last of the five evenings; content not detailed in the sources we read 
 Source: Sorrisi, republishing the Rai rules , checked on 16 November 2026. 
 The casting follows a firm timetable. Twenty-four artists will compete, 23 chosen by the artistic director and the winner of Sanremo Giovani 2026. Proposals must reach Rai before 23 November 2026, and names can only be announced from 29 November 2026. Names already circulating were not confirmed as of 16 November, so wait for the official announcement before you take them as fact.
 The 2027 Eurovision calendar has not been set in the sources we could read. According to the press (ITV, 13 August 2026), the 2027 edition would be held in Burgas, Bulgaria, in the week of 11 to 15 May 2027; the organiser has not confirmed this in the sources we read. The official contest site was not accessible when we checked, so don’t plan your trip around a Eurovision date until one is published.
 3. Tickets for the Ariston: procedure and 2026 prices
 A lottery-based sale, with no date for 2027
 Platea: €240 per evening (2026) 
 2027 sale: December 2026 
 2 tickets maximum 
 Teatro Ariston The 2027 sale has no confirmed day yet. According to Open , which cites a Rai warning of 7 November 2026, sales will start in December. The same warning cautions against platforms and unauthorised sites. Fake tickets are circulating, so the safest route is to buy only through the channels Rai designates.
 How it worked in 2026
 Online registration on Vivaticket from 22 December 2025 to 8 January 2026. 
 Lottery drawn in front of a notary, then an invitation to buy sent between 15 January and 3 February. 
 Two tickets maximum per person, named, with photo ID shown at the entrance. No box office sales. 
 Pixidia tip: don’t count on a last-minute ticket. In 2026, public access went through online registration followed by a lottery; no other route is documented in the sources we read, and seats remain highly sought after. Teatro Ariston tickets 2026, prices published by the press (unofficial, no 2027 prices published) Zone Evenings 1 to 4 Final evening Five-evening pass 
 Platea €240 €875 €1,835 
 Galleria €132 €430 €958 
 Source: Radiotime (5 February 2026) and Money.it (24 February 2026), checked on 16 November 2026. 
 The five-evening pass is the sum of the five evenings. Money.it mentions a rise of around 20% on previous editions, without citing an official source for that figure. The theatre holds about 2,000 seats, and a large share goes to guests, sponsors and professionals, so public demand far exceeds supply.
 Outside the hall, the area is controlled. In 2026, red and yellow zones surrounded the Ariston, with car parks linked by shuttle buses at €20 per day, according to Italian Riviera , in its update of 24 October 2026. The 2027 rules have not been published, so check before you drive.
 4. Where to stay: an expensive week and nearby towns
 Photo by Annie Spratt on Unsplash Hotels almost full, rentals expensive
 Week: from €600 (Airbnb) 
 Simulation for 14 to 21 February 2027 
 Hotels nearby: almost full 
 Bordighera: about 8 min by train Lifestyleblog ran a search on 7 June 2026 for one person from 14 to 21 February 2027. The cheapest option on Booking started at about €1,611 for the week, and on Airbnb between €600 and €660. These are weekly totals, not nightly rates, and they were checked several months before the Festival. According to the same source, hotels near the Ariston are almost all full.
 Pixidia tip: if you want a room for the week, widen your search now to nearby towns. Hotel rates for February 2027 have not been published. Accommodation for one person for the Festival week, June 2026 simulation (14 to 21 February 2027) Platform Cheapest option Typical option Top-end option 
 Booking from about €1,611 not specified over €60,000 (Lifestyleblog simulation, one person, one week) 
 Airbnb €600 to €660 €1,500 to €2,600 over €3,700 
 Source: Lifestyleblog , article of 7 June 2026, checked on 16 November 2026. 
 The Hotel des Anglais announces the 2027 Festival on its website, without publishing a rate. No official hotel rate for the week was found.
 Nearby towns are cited in several sources as fallback options: Ventimiglia, Bordighera and Ospedaletti. No hotel rate for the week is sourced for these towns. Bordighera is about 8 minutes by train from Sanremo, but staying further away means train trips back in the evening, so plan your timetable before you go.
 The tourist tax is not priced in this article, because the rate that applies in Sanremo was not found in the sources we read. A proposal reported by Open on 26 October 2026 would exempt Festival artists from 2027. At this stage, it does not concern the public.
 5. Indicative budget: the published costs
 The table below lists the published costs without adding them into a total: each amount carries its date and source. The five-evening pass is the sum of the evenings, with no discount: 4 × €240 + €875 = €1,835. The costs are not added into a total stay, because accommodation and meals depend on your profile. A solo traveller staying in Bordighera spends differently from a couple booking in Sanremo.
 Published budget items for a Festival stay, checked on 16 November 2026 Item Amount Source and date 
 Platea ticket, one evening (2026) €240 Radiotime, 5 February 2026 
 Galleria ticket, one evening (2026) €132 Radiotime, 5 February 2026 
 Platea five-evening pass (2026) €1,835 Money.it, 24 February 2026 
 One-week accommodation, cheapest Airbnb option €600 to €660 Lifestyleblog, 7 June 2026 
 One-week accommodation, cheapest Booking option from about €1,611 Lifestyleblog, 7 June 2026 
 Parking and shuttle around the Ariston (2026) €20 per day Italian Riviera, 24 October 2026 
 Sanremo Food Tour (base 2 adults) €190 for 2 adults (€95 per adult) Viator, checked on 16 November 2026 
 Train Nice to Ventimiglia (TER) about €10.20 train aggregators (unofficial), 16 November 2026 
 Genova Airlink shuttle, Genoa airport to Sestri Ponente €2 Trenitalia, checked on 16 November 2026 
 Amounts published by the sources cited, checked on 16 November 2026. 2027 prices have not been published. 
 This budget excludes meals, the tourist tax (not priced) and the outbound journey. One research firm offers a benchmark: EY estimates an average daily spend of about €500 per spectator, including transport, accommodation and food, with a 90% occupancy rate over the five evenings (press release of 13 February 2026). It is an assumption used for an economic impact calculation, not a travel budget.
 To keep costs down, two levers are backed by sources. Staying in a nearby town can reduce the accommodation bill, provided you check a rate for the week that we did not find. Staying in town during the week, as described in section 1, takes the ticket cost down to zero.
 6. Getting to Sanremo by train
 Sanremo sits on the Ligurian coastal line. The timetables and fares below come from train aggregators (Omio, Trainline, Virail) and travel guides, not from operators. Check them before you book, as connections change by day.
 Trains to Sanremo, indicative durations and fares checked on 16 November 2026 (aggregators, unofficial) Route Indicative duration Indicative fare Source 
 Nice to Ventimiglia (TER) 48 min to 1 h 20 about €10.20 aggregators (unofficial) 
 Ventimiglia to Sanremo about 20 min not found aggregators (unofficial) 
 Bordighera to Sanremo about 8 min not found aggregators (unofficial) 
 Milan to Sanremo 3 h 51 at the fastest, about 4 h 30 in practice €17.90 to €47.10 Omio, Trainline (unofficial) 
 Paris to Sanremo 8 h 16 to 12 h 30, with a change at Ventimiglia not found Omio, Virail, Trainline (unofficial) 
 Genoa airport to Sestri Ponente about 5 min by shuttle €2 (shuttle) Trenitalia (Genova Airlink) 
 Sources: Omio, Trainline and Virail train aggregators, the Seat61 travel guide and Trenitalia’s Genova Airlink page, checked on 16 November 2026. 
 From Nice, take a TER to Ventimiglia, then an Italian train to Sanremo. These are two separate tickets, with a border crossing. From Paris, there is no direct train: the journey goes through Ventimiglia and takes between 8 hours and 12 h 30, according to the aggregators.
 From Genoa airport, the Genova Airlink shuttle reaches Genova Sestri Ponente station in about five minutes, for €2. You then need a regional train to Sanremo: its duration was not checked in the sources we read, so allow plenty of time. By car, the A10, the Autostrada dei Fiori, runs along the coast. Parking around the Ariston was controlled in 2026, as noted above, and the 2027 rules have not been published.
 Border checks with Italy can tighten depending on the period. We could not confirm the status of these checks for February 2027: check the UK government’s travel advice for Italy before you leave.
 7. February in Sanremo: cool, damp and a chilly sea
 February is the coldest month of the year in Sanremo. The 2004 to 2020 averages give about 8°C at minimum and 13°C at maximum, with the sea at about 13°C. The town gets about 65 mm of rain on roughly 5 days on average. Snow is very rare on the coast.
 Climate in Sanremo in February, 2004 to 2020 averages Indicator Value 
 Average minimum about 8°C 
 Average maximum about 13°C 
 Average temperature about 10.6°C 
 Sea temperature about 13°C 
 Rain about 65 mm over roughly 5 days 
 Source: Climi e Viaggi (2004 to 2020 averages), checked on 16 November 2026. 
 For the Festival, that means cool evenings and walks between the centre, the seafront and the Ariston. Pack a waterproof jacket (about 65 mm of rain on average over roughly 5 days), shoes that cope with wet pavement, and an extra layer for the time spent outside while waiting for the red carpet.
 8. Tailoring your stay to your profile
 The Festival looks different depending on who is going. The advice below reflects Pixidia’s choices, based on the sourced facts above, not official recommendations.
 First time, no ticket
 Focus your stay on the town: La Pigna in the morning, Corso Imperatrice in the afternoon, and the free evening events if they return. You’ll feel the Festival’s atmosphere without relying on a seat at the Ariston, which remains a lottery.
 Tight budget
 Look first at Bordighera or Ventimiglia as fallback options. No hotel rate for the week is sourced for these towns, but Bordighera is about 8 minutes by train from Sanremo. The hotel rate for the week is not published, so compare several platforms before you book a room. Keep the ticket cost at zero if you didn’t win the lottery.
 Couple or small group
 The limit of two tickets per person, issued in each person’s name, means you need to travel with the exact people whose ID you carry. Book accommodation before the end of the year, as hotels near the Ariston are almost fully booked.
 Family with children
 The Festival evenings run late, and February is cold. A room in the centre avoids late-night journeys, while a nearby town suits you if you have a car. In 2026, a galleria ticket cost €132 an evening, and the events took place outdoors in the town. For a young child, the town alone can fill a week; a guided tour of the Ariston, priced at €9 (€6 for ages 6 to 12, probably a 2024 rate and to be checked), is another option.
 Reduced mobility
 Sanremo’s centre mixes narrow streets, cobbles and steps, notably in La Pigna. The red and yellow zones around the Ariston in 2026 required parking and shuttles. Before you book, check the accessibility of the accommodation and routes, as no accessibility data was found in the sources.
 9. Mistakes to avoid
 A few pitfalls come up again and again in guides and in the press. Avoiding them costs less than discovering them on the spot.
 Buying a ticket from a resale site. Rai’s warning cautions against fake tickets and unauthorised platforms. 
 Waiting for a January sale. Some guides repeat this; Rai refers to December 2026, with no set day. 
 Taking the 2026 programme for granted. The Green Carpet and the Piazza Colombo concerts are benchmarks, not commitments for 2027. 
 Booking a Paris to Sanremo trip with no change at Ventimiglia. There is no direct train. 
 Forgetting photo ID. Your passport is the safe choice: photo ID is checked at the theatre entrance, and border checks apply at the frontier. 
 10. What other guides don’t tell you
 The guides we read (aggregators, hotel pages, unofficial sites) contain several errors or gaps. Here are the points we checked, with source and date of consultation.
 The 2027 sale has a month, not a day. Some guides say January, but Rai refers to December with no day given. Open , relaying a Rai warning of 7 November 2026, checked 16 November 2026.
 The site sanremofestival.it is not an official site. Don’t cite it as a source for dates or tickets. Our research, checked on 16 November 2026, found that this site’s name does not match an official Rai source.
 The performance night on 19 February selects Italy’s Eurovision representative. This change of format does not appear in the guides we read. Sorrisi , republishing the Rai rules of 21 September 2026, checked 16 November 2026.
 Online voting is limited to three votes per user. The weighting between online votes and the jury is not confirmed: no percentage is given here. Sorrisi , checked 16 November 2026.
 The Green Carpet and Piazza Colombo are 2026 benchmarks, not guarantees for 2027. The guides cite them without a date. Italpress, for the 2026 edition, checked 16 November 2026.
 The ban on AI-written songs does not describe any detection method. The text is a rule, not a technical system. LaPresse , 21 September 2026, checked 16 November 2026.
 11. Practical information
 Entry formalities. British citizens don’t need a visa for tourist stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen area, which includes Italy. Your passport must have been issued less than 10 years before you arrive and must expire at least 3 months after the day you plan to leave the Schengen area, according to the UK government’s Italy travel advice . That page refers to a full British passport and does not mention identity cards, so travel with your passport.
 Border checks. The EU’s Entry/Exit System (EES) is being rolled out across the Schengen area. Expect fingerprints and a photo at your first crossing and possibly longer waits, since it replaces passport stamping.
 Tickets. Buy only through the channels designated by Rai. In 2026, the process relied on online registration, a lottery and a maximum of two named tickets.
 Access to the theatre. The Teatro Ariston is in the centre of Sanremo. Parking around the hall was controlled in 2026.
 Frequently asked questions
 What are the dates of the Sanremo Festival 2027? The Festival runs from Tuesday 16 to Saturday 20 February 2027, over five evenings at the Teatro Ariston. These dates come from the rules published by Rai on 21 September 2026, relayed by Sorrisi . The cover night falls on Thursday 18, the performance night on Friday 19 and the final night on Saturday 20.
 How do you buy tickets for the Sanremo Festival? In 2026, access went through online registration followed by a lottery. Registration on Vivaticket ran from 22 December 2025 to 8 January 2026, with a maximum of two named tickets and photo ID shown at the entrance. The 2027 procedure has not yet been published in detail, and the sale announced for December 2026 has no set day.
 When do the Sanremo 2027 tickets go on sale? There is no official date. According to Open , which cites a Rai warning of 7 November 2026, sales should start in December 2026, without a set day. Answers that mention January are not based on this source.
 How much do Sanremo Festival tickets cost? The 2027 prices have not been published. In 2026, the press listed €132 per evening in the galleria and €240 in the platea for the first four evenings, €875 for the final evening in the platea, and €1,835 for the five-evening pass, according to Radiotime . These figures are not official prices.
 Can you attend the Festival without a ticket? Partly. In 2026, the Green Carpet ran along Via Matteotti and Piazza Colombo hosted free concerts. The 2027 programme has not been published, so check the events on the day. The Festival is also broadcast on television, on Rai channels.
 Where should you stay in Sanremo during the Festival? Hotels near the Ariston are almost all full, according to Lifestyleblog (June 2026). Ventimiglia, Bordighera and Ospedaletti are cited as fallback options. For the week, the cheapest accommodation found started at about €600 on Airbnb, with no hotel rate published for February 2027.
 How do you get from Nice to Sanremo by train? Take the TER to Ventimiglia, which takes about 48 minutes to 1 h 20 according to aggregators, for about €10.20. You then need an Italian train to Sanremo, allow about 20 minutes. The two tickets are separate, with a border crossing.
 How do you get from Paris to Sanremo? There is no direct train. The journey goes through Ventimiglia and takes between 8 hours and 12 h 30 according to the Omio, Virail and Trainline aggregators. Flying to Genoa is an option: the Genova Airlink shuttle costs €2 to Sestri Ponente, then a regional train whose duration was not checked.
 Do you need a visa for Italy? No. For a British passport holder, a valid passport is enough for tourist stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period in the Schengen area. The UK government’s Italy travel advice is the reference. Still check the border control conditions before you travel.
 What is the weather like in Sanremo in February? The 2004 to 2020 averages give about 8°C at minimum and 13°C at maximum, with a sea at about 13°C and about 65 mm of rain over the period. Snow is very rare on the coast. A waterproof jacket is the best kit for evenings spent outdoors.
 Sources

 LaPresse, « Sanremo 2027, ecco il Festival di De Martino »  : performance night and AI rules, 21 September 2026.

 Omio, Trainline and Virail : train aggregators, unofficial, checked 16 November 2026. Seat61, travel guide to train journeys from France.

 Sources checked on 16 November 2026. The websites of Rai and Eurovision were not readable at the time of research: the rules are cited as reported by the press. The 2026 prices are published by the press, not by the official ticket office.
